audit.why: 45.97% over 385 games — the only losing matchup in this slice, and the only one where the level chart is honest about it: every stage reads Skill except first item, which is Locke's. The prose matches, calling it 'an even but twitchy lane' with his first item as the danger stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 line said 'base ults roughly trade' without either number, and Ashen Pursuit — described in the full layer as the cooldown the whole lane turns on — had no duration.
audit.why: Purgatory and Petrifying Gaze are both 120s at rank 1, so 'roughly trade' is exactly right and can be said precisely. Ashen Pursuit is 10s flat and Ritual Nails 10s at rank 1 falling to 6s. A page built around 'the post-E window is the lane' has to say how long that window is.
audit.corrected: 120s written into content.spikes[1].text; 10s and 6s into content.early, full.breakdown.cooldowns and full.loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly says to drop W 'on his approach path' and calls it 'your grounding W', but never once states what the grounding actually does to him.
audit.why: Riot: Ashen Pursuit 'teleports to a location before dashing to attack his next target' — a movement ability, and per the full layer's own cooldown note his ONLY mobility. Grounded enemies cannot use movement abilities, so a single Miasma removes his engage and his escape at the same time. That is the strongest thing Cassiopeia does in this matchup and it was implied rather than said, which is why the flank fear in spikes[2] and mid reads as unanswerable when it is not.
audit.corrected: Named explicitly in content.spikes[0].text, content.early, content.mid, content.whys[2], full.report[5].t, full.breakdown.cooldowns and full.loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.report[8].t states 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Grievous Wounds reduces healing by source-agnostic rule, and Soul Ignition is a heal: Riot says 'at the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect.' Calling a heal 'not lifesteal' does not make it immune to anti-heal, and telling a losing-matchup reader to skip the item that blunts his recovery is the wrong call.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now recommends anti-heal and names Soul Ignition as the reason. The Zhonya's-versus-Purgatory advice on the same line is untouched — it is good and I could not fault it.

notes: This is the one losing matchup in the slice and the one whose page was already the most honest — no fabricated ability names, no invented power shifts, and a level chart that says 'Skill' six times rather than pretending. The gap was that the single mechanic that makes the lane survivable, Miasma grounding his only blink, was implied on every panel and stated on none. Two things I did not touch: full.tldr calls him 'a 125-range mana champ' — the kit carries no attack-range figure, so I cannot confirm or deny 125; and full.report[5]'s claim that his blink 'resets on takedowns' is not in Riot's text either. Both are in unverified. Purgatory does apply grounding itself per the kit, but Cassiopeia owns no dash, so writing that would be a non-interaction and the applier would rightly reject it.
